svg.text: Hook chain — what runs, what it stops, and what makes it inert
Thirteen scripts across two registration channels. Every entry is rooted at ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} and runs with timeout: 10.
GROUPED BY WHAT MAKES A HOOK INERT — NOT BY WHERE IT IS REGISTERED
An unconditional wall reads the tool payload and nothing else, so it can refuse in any session on this machine, armed or not. A run-state-gated wall reads canonical-sdlc state
on disk — a plan under the plan dirs, or this session's roster file — and exits 0 in silence outside an active run. REGISTERED says where each registration lives; that is a
separate fact, and it is not what decides the lane. plugin = payload/hooks/hooks.json, installed with the plugin. skill = the hooks: block in ../SKILL.md frontmatter.
UNCONDITIONAL
four walls that read only the payload — they can refuse on any session, in any project, whether or not canonical-sdlc was ever invoked.
WHAT RUNS
REGISTERED
ARM
WHAT IT STOPS
protect-main.sh
plugin PreToolUse · Bash
BLOCK · exit 2
A git push to main or master. The command is split on && / || / ; and only real command segments are read, so a
commit message that happens to mention pushing is not a hit. The user pushes to main from their own terminal.
protect-database.sh
plugin PreToolUse · Bash
BLOCK · exit 2
DROP, TRUNCATE, ALTER TABLE … DROP, and a DELETE with no WHERE — through psql, mysql, sqlite3 and the
other common database CLIs. It reads the command text and nothing else, not even the branch.
farm-out-reminder.sh
skill PreToolUse · Bash
DENY · via JSON
A long-running main-thread command — the full test suite, the bootstrap — denied with a redirect naming the role
that should run it; fuzzy matches get one nudge per class per session. Exit 0 always: the decision is stdout JSON.
canonical-sdlc-governing-skill.sh
plugin PreToolUse · Write ↳ via guard
plugin PreToolUse · Edit ↳ via guard
skill PreToolUse · Write, Edit
BLOCK · exit 2
An artifact under <docs-root>/{specs,plans,adrs,incidents}/ that fails the ladder below — the full frontmatter
contract, plus the three-way design rule on a wave-or-epic spec. It validates Write CONTENT only, so one valid
write covers every later edit of that file: a known hole, listed at the bottom of this page rather than discovered.
RUN-STATE-GATED
nine scripts that read canonical-sdlc state on disk first and exit 0 in silence when it is absent — outside a run they are no-ops.
WHAT RUNS
REGISTERED
ARM
WHAT IT DOES · AND WHAT SILENCES IT
agent-context-guard.sh
gate: roster-<session_id>.state
plugin fronts five entries above
— never registered alone
PASS-THROUGH
The channel partition — why four plugin entries point here and not straight at a wall. A skill-frontmatter hook is looked
up by SESSION id, so it is invisible from inside an agent; the plugin channel is alive in both places and would double-fire.
So it execs the wall handed to it by argument only when the payload carries an agent_id AND the session roster exists.
Anything else, ambiguity included, exits 0 in silence: a refusal nobody wrote would be blamed on the wall behind it.
dispatch-preflight.sh
gate: active-wave plan
plugin PreToolUse · Agent ↳ via guard
skill PreToolUse · Agent
BLOCK · exit 2
A dispatch, during an active wave, with no this-session environment attestation — or whose brief names no single
Expected artifact: path (zero refuses to name one, more than one refuses to choose). This is also the arm that writes
the session roster row, which is why the guard hands the agent-context copy a flag to skip that part.
background-suite-guard.sh
gate: agent_id + armed roster (subagent only)
plugin PreToolUse · Bash ↳ via guard
BLOCK · exit 2
A subagent's own Bash call carrying run_in_background: true on a suite-class command (bash tests/run.sh, pytest,
npm test …) inside an armed session — refused, naming the foreground form: … 2>&1 | tee <evidence log>.
The same command foreground, a non-suite command, or a main-thread payload with no agent_id passes untouched.
landing-gate.sh
gate: roster, then the plan
plugin SubagentStop ↳ via guard
skill Stop
BLOCK · once
The landing sweep: a verdict for every contract that has landed since the last sweep — reached at the orchestrator's
own turn end on Stop, and from inside an agent on SubagentStop. It refuses the stop exactly once when one of those
contracts named an artifact that is not on disk, then lets the next one through.
canonical-sdlc-evidence-gate.sh
gate: a plan's ## SDLC State
skill PreToolUse · Bash
BLOCK · exit 2
The commit wall; its ladder is below. It fires only on a real git commit segment (quote-aware), so every other Bash
command passes untouched. With no plan under the plan dirs it still sweeps for a MISPLACED one, so it is fully inert
only when the project holds no canonical-sdlc plan at all — the one hook here whose gate is not a clean early exit.
stop-guard.sh
gate: active-wave plan
skill PreToolUse · TaskStop
BLOCK · exit 2
A stop backed by no fresh observation, by a spent one, or by another actor's borrowed look — and a stop of a target
this session never launched, when addressed by name. The full agent id is the deliberate path past that refusal.
execution-recorder.sh
gate: plan, then the roster
skill PostToolUse · Bash, Agent
skill SubagentStart
RECORD
Three arms on one script. OBSERVATION (Bash): when stop-check.sh has printed its machine line, that line becomes
the record a later stop is allowed to spend — one observation, exactly one stop. ROSTER (Agent): a dispatch that
actually spawned completes its intended row, status confirmed. IDENTIFICATION (SubagentStart): the agent's own
transcript-form id joins the roster BY THAT ID — not by name, and not by the agent_type, which made the join collide.
context-spend.sh
gate: a plan with a step
skill Stop
LOG ONLY
One context-spend line per SDLC step boundary. A missing jq, transcript, usage block or plan means exit 0 and
silence; it never writes stdout at all, because a Stop hook's stdout could be read as a block payload.
patrol-duties-gate.sh
gate: Patrol-tick duties
skill Stop
BLOCK · once
Refuses a Patrol-tick turn's end, once, unless both standing duties ran since the tick fired — a
subagent-panel refresh and a task-list refresh. Any other turn passes untouched.
THE TWO SDLC LADDERS — first failure wins, and it names itself
canonical-sdlc-governing-skill.sh
PreToolUse · Write, Edit — the artifact wall
the path is under <docs-root>/{specs,plans,adrs,incidents}/
governing-skill: is present in the frontmatter
canonical_sdlc_version == 14
the triple is present and enum-valid — intent · rigor · scale
no mode: line, and the intent × scale cell is not barred
flags and model_plan present; walk: is required or exempt
## Verification Matrix present once sdlc-step ≥ 3
a wave-or-epic SPEC satisfies one design arm: a flush-left ## Design
in place, a design: pointer that resolves to a file carrying one, or a
design-waived: token
All pass → the Write proceeds. Any failure → exit 2, and the file is never written.
LOG-ONLY: rigor-floor consistency — and it logs user-overridden rather than a
violation when rigor-override: is present. Plans and task-scale artifacts are untouched.
canonical-sdlc-evidence-gate.sh
PreToolUse · Bash — the commit wall, on real git commit segments only
newest plan under the plan dirs → its ## SDLC State, fence-aware
canonical_sdlc_version == 14
current: N — or current: T<n> at scale: task
Step N's evidence keys present, and none of them a placeholder
(todo · pending · in progress · xxx · tbd · placeholder all reject)
at Step 5: cmd / pass / total / output with pass == total, a valid
## Verification Matrix, and a non-empty auditor: once no row is pending
from current: 5 onward — no AC block says provenance: implementation
from current: 5 onward — walk-artifact: resolves to a real file under
<docs-root>/record/ and names the AC (unless walk: exempt)
Valid → the commit proceeds. Otherwise → exit 2, and git never runs.
LOG-ONLY: the epic merge-target check, and the intent-scoped Step-5 keys for
refactor (behavior-preservation · compat-matrix · revert-plan) and tune (baseline · target · re-measure).
ONE SUPPORTED VERSION
canonical_sdlc_version: 14 is the only value either hook accepts.
Anything else — older, empty, malformed — exits 2 naming the value it
found. No grandfathering. This page's three renderings are pinned to it.
THE LOG-ONLY SIDE CHANNEL
$HOME/.claude/logs/<project-slug>/sdlc-audit.md
Deliberately outside every consuming project tree. One line per finding
plus an stderr echo, and it never blocks the wave.
KNOWN HOLES — NOT ENFORCEMENT
The artifact wall validates Write content, not Edit content. Flag VALUES
are never checked, only presence. The evidence gate reads the plan's text,
so an Edit writing evidence for tests never run passes unseen.
